summary: This section of the Foot Locker, Inc. Form 8-K filed on August 19, 2022, details significant leadership changes, including the resignation of Richard A. Johnson as President and CEO and the appointment of Mary N. Dillon as his successor. It outlines the terms of their employment agreements, including severance provisions, indemnification, and confidentiality obligations. Additionally, it defines 'Change in Control' scenarios relevant to the company and includes forward-looking statements regarding future activities. The section emphasizes compliance with legal frameworks, particularly Section 409A, and includes provisions for arbitration and dispute resolution.

children.title: Form 8-K Front Matter for Foot Locker, Inc.
children.summary: This section contains the front matter for Form 8-K, a current report filed with the SEC by Foot Locker, Inc. It includes essential details such as the date of the report, the registrant's name, jurisdiction of incorporation, and contact information. The section also provides options for indicating if the filing serves multiple purposes under various SEC rules. Additionally, it lists the securities registered and their trading symbol on the New York Stock Exchange, along with a checkbox for the emerging growth company status.

children.title: Leadership Changes and Employment Agreements at Foot Locker
children.summary: On August 19, 2022, Foot Locker, Inc. announced the resignation of Richard A. Johnson as President and CEO, effective September 1, 2022, with Mary N. Dillon appointed as his successor. Dillon's extensive background includes leadership roles at Ulta Beauty and United States Cellular Corporation. The section details Johnson's transition agreement, including his role as Executive Chairman and reduced salary, and outlines Dillon's employment agreement, which includes a base salary of $1.3 million, a cash sign-on bonus, and various equity awards. The agreements are designed to facilitate a smooth leadership transition and incentivize performance.

children.title: Severance Terms and Exhibit Listings
children.summary: This section outlines the severance terms for Ms. Dillon under her Employment Agreement with Foot Locker, Inc., detailing conditions for severance payments, including base salary continuation, pro-rated bonuses, and outplacement services. It specifies the vesting conditions for equity awards based on the timing of her employment termination. Additionally, it lists the exhibits included in the filing, such as employment agreements and a press release. The section concludes with a signature from the company's General Counsel, affirming compliance with the Securities Exchange Act of 1934.

children.title: Letter Agreement for CEO Transition and Retirement
children.summary: This section outlines the Letter Agreement between Richard A. Johnson and Foot Locker, Inc. regarding his retirement and transition to Executive Chairman and later Senior Advisor roles. It details the terms of his employment during the transition, including compensation, responsibilities, and benefits. The agreement also includes provisions on post-termination obligations, non-solicitation, and cooperation with the company after retirement. Additionally, it addresses legal fees, indemnification, and compliance with Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code.

children.title: Employment Agreement for President and CEO Mary N. Dillon
children.summary: This section contains the Employment Agreement between Foot Locker, Inc. and Mary N. Dillon, detailing her role as President and CEO starting August 19, 2022, with an initial term ending January 31, 2026. It outlines the terms of employment, including automatic renewal provisions, and specifies that Dillon will serve in a non-executive advisory capacity until September 1, 2022. The agreement also mandates her election to the Board of Directors within 30 days of the commencement date and describes her responsibilities and authority as CEO, including the requirement to devote full working time to the company.

children.title: Employment Agreement for CEO Mary N. Dillon
children.summary: The Employment Agreement section details the terms of Mary N. Dillon's role as President and CEO of Foot Locker, Inc., including her employment duration, responsibilities, compensation structure, and additional benefits. It specifies her initial advisory role, location of employment, cash compensation, equity awards, and conditions for termination. The section also outlines the obligations of both the Executive and the Company upon termination, including severance conditions and implications of a Change in Control.

children.title: Employment Agreement Details for CEO Mary N. Dillon
children.summary: This section outlines the employment agreement between Foot Locker, Inc. and Mary N. Dillon, detailing her role as President and CEO. The employment commences on August 19, 2022, and lasts until January 31, 2026, with automatic one-year renewals unless terminated with 180 days' notice. It specifies that Dillon will be elected to the Board of Directors within 30 days of the start date and describes her initial advisory role before assuming full responsibilities as CEO on September 1, 2022.

children.title: Executive Position and Responsibilities
children.summary: This section outlines the position and duties of Mary N. Dillon as President and Chief Executive Officer of Foot Locker, Inc. It specifies that she will initially serve in a non-executive advisory role until September 1, 2022, after which she will report directly to the Board of Directors. The section details her responsibilities, which include devoting her full working time to the company and potentially serving as an officer or director of its subsidiaries. Additionally, it states that upon termination of her employment, she will resign from all positions held within the company.

children.title: Location of Executive's Employment and Travel Requirements
children.summary: This section specifies that the Executive will perform services from an office located in the Chicago, Illinois area, with the requirement to travel as necessary for their role. It outlines the location of performance as a key aspect of the Executive's employment agreement, emphasizing the importance of the Chicago area for the company's operations. Additionally, it indicates that the Executive's responsibilities may involve travel related to their position.

children.title: Executive Cash Compensation Details
children.summary: This section outlines the cash compensation structure for the Executive during the Employment Period. It specifies a minimum base salary of $1,300,000 per year, which will be paid in monthly installments and reviewed annually by the Compensation Committee. Additionally, the Executive is entitled to participate in various bonus, incentive, and equity plans available to senior executives, with the possibility of amendments or terminations to these plans as long as they apply uniformly to all comparably situated executives.

children.title: Inducement and Equity Awards for Executive
children.summary: This section outlines the inducement and equity awards provided to the Executive upon commencement of employment. It details the Employment Inducement Award consisting of restricted stock units (RSUs) and performance-based stock units (PSUs), including their vesting schedules and performance metrics. Additionally, it describes an initial annual equity grant valued at $8,000,000, allocated among PSUs, stock options, and RSUs, along with eligibility for annual equity awards under the Company’s Stock Plan. Specific vesting provisions are also included, particularly regarding voluntary termination of employment.

children.title: Overview of Executive Additional Benefits and Perks
children.summary: This section outlines additional benefits for the Executive during their employment, including eligibility for pension and welfare plans, life insurance equal to their annual salary, long-term disability insurance, medical expense reimbursement, and a financial planning allowance. It specifies that the Executive will receive a sign-on bonus of $250,000 and reimbursement for reasonable business expenses. The section also details vacation entitlements and reimbursement for legal fees related to the employment agreement, capped at $40,000. Definitions of comparably situated senior executives are provided for clarity.

children.title: Termination Conditions and Obligations
children.summary: This section outlines the conditions under which the Executive's employment may be terminated, including termination by the Company for Cause or without Cause, and termination by the Executive for Good Reason. It specifies the obligations of the Company upon termination, including payment of Base Salary, reimbursement of expenses, and any vested benefits. Additionally, it details the conditions for receiving severance payments, including the requirement for the Executive to sign a release of claims. The section also addresses the implications of a Change in Control on termination benefits and outlines provisions to avoid excess parachute payments under tax regulations.

children.title: Indemnification Provisions for Executive
children.summary: This section outlines the indemnification provisions for the Executive, ensuring that she is entitled to benefits as specified in the Company's Certificate of Incorporation and By-laws during and after her employment. It includes the Company's commitment to maintain directors' and officers' liability insurance for the Executive, covering her actions as an officer or director. Additionally, it states that an Indemnification Agreement will be executed with the Executive effective from the Commencement Date.

children.title: Confidentiality and Non-Competition Obligations
children.summary: This section outlines the Executive's obligations regarding Confidential Information and non-competition during and after employment. It defines Confidential Information as nonpublic data related to the Company's operations, finances, and strategies, which the Executive must not disclose or use without consent. The Executive is prohibited from engaging in competition with the Company for two years post-employment, including soliciting employees or providing similar services to competitors. The section emphasizes the importance of these obligations to protect the Company's interests and allows for legal enforcement through injunctions if violated.

children.title: Assignment and Arbitration Provisions
children.summary: This section outlines the assignment of rights and obligations under the Agreement, specifying that the Executive cannot assign her rights, while the Company can assign its rights in certain circumstances, such as mergers or asset sales. It also details the arbitration process for resolving disputes related to the Agreement, including employment-related claims and discrimination issues, with arbitration to occur in New York. Additionally, it describes the notice requirements for communication between the parties and states that the Agreement is governed by New York law, with jurisdiction in New York courts.

children.title: Arbitration Process and Dispute Resolution
children.summary: This section outlines the arbitration process for resolving disputes related to the Agreement, including employment-related claims and allegations of discrimination or harassment. It specifies that arbitration will occur in New York City under the rules of the American Arbitration Association (AAA), with costs shared equally by both parties. The section also clarifies that certain claims, such as those related to sexual harassment or assault, may not be subject to arbitration if prohibited by law. The decision of the arbitrator(s) is final and binding, and the section includes provisions for notice and applicable law governing the Agreement.

children.title: Legal Framework and Compliance Provisions
children.summary: This section outlines the legal framework regarding the enforcement of the agreement, specifically addressing the waiver of the defense of inconvenient forum. It details compliance with Section 409A, including definitions of 'termination' and the implications for specified employees regarding deferred compensation. The section also stipulates the conditions for reimbursement of expenses and the timing of payments. Additionally, it includes the Executive's representation of legal capacity to enter the agreement and emphasizes that this document constitutes the entire agreement between the parties, with provisions for amendments and waivers.

children.title: Overview of Applicable Law and Compliance Requirements
children.summary: This section outlines the applicable law governing the agreement, emphasizing compliance with Section 409A regarding deferred compensation. It specifies that if the Executive is classified as a 'specified employee', payments will be delayed for six months post-termination. Additionally, it details the treatment of reimbursements and in-kind benefits to ensure they align with tax regulations. The section also includes representations by the Executive regarding legal compliance and the agreement's status as the entire understanding between the parties, requiring written amendments for any changes.

children.title: Compliance with Section 409A for Deferred Compensation
children.summary: Section 409A outlines the intent for compliance with Section 409A regarding deferred compensation payments under the Agreement. It specifies that if the Executive is classified as a 'specified employee', payments due to termination of employment will be delayed for six months post-separation. Additionally, it details the rules for reimbursement of expenses, ensuring they are not liquidated or exchanged for other benefits and must be paid within a specific timeframe. The section also clarifies that there are no guarantees regarding the tax consequences of these payments.

children.title: Enforcement and Withholding Provisions
children.summary: This section outlines the enforcement of provisions within the agreement, stating that the failure to enforce a provision does not waive the right to enforce it later. It clarifies that a waiver of a breach does not imply a continuing waiver for future breaches. Additionally, it specifies that the Company is permitted to withhold taxes from payments as required by law. Lastly, it notes that section headings are for reference only and do not influence the agreement's interpretation.

children.title: Legal Provisions and Signatures
children.summary: This section outlines the legal stipulations regarding the enforcement of the agreement, emphasizing that a party's failure to enforce a provision does not waive their right to do so in the future. It also specifies that the Company is permitted to withhold necessary taxes from payments as required by law. Additionally, it clarifies that section headings are for reference only and do not influence the interpretation of the agreement. The section concludes with the signatures of the parties involved, formalizing the agreement.

children.title: Definition of Change in Control
children.summary: This section defines 'Change in Control' for the Company, outlining specific scenarios that qualify as such. It includes conditions like mergers or asset sales that result in a shift of ownership, acquisitions of 35% or more of voting securities by any person, and changes in the majority of the Board of Directors within a year. The definition is aligned with regulatory standards under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and aims to clarify what constitutes a significant change in corporate control or asset ownership.

children.title: Definition of Change in Control for the Company
children.summary: Attachment A defines 'Change in Control' for the Company, outlining specific scenarios that qualify, including mergers, acquisitions of significant ownership stakes, and changes in board composition. It specifies that a merger is not considered a change if the original voting securities maintain majority representation. The section also details the thresholds for ownership changes and the implications for corporate governance under Section 409A. This definition is crucial for understanding the conditions under which control of the Company may shift, impacting stakeholders and governance.

children.title: Forward-Looking Statements Disclosure
children.summary: This section outlines that the press release includes forward-looking statements as defined by federal securities laws, which pertain to anticipated future activities and developments of Foot Locker, Inc. It specifies that these statements cover areas such as capital expenditures, strategic plans, and financial objectives. The section emphasizes that these statements are based on assumptions and are subject to various risks and uncertainties, which are detailed in the company's SEC filings. It also notes that Foot Locker, Inc. does not commit to updating these statements in light of new information or events.
